open_points.subject: A09 rule 2 multipart request construction
open_points.text: "A binding with a `file` input sends, for `POST`, `PUT` and `PATCH`, a `multipart/form-data` body with one part per other input port named by the port — one part per file, in list order, for a `many` file port"
open_points.question: When several input ports are present, in what exact order must multipart parts be emitted (across ports and files) so different implementations produce the same wire request?
options: Port-name order, with each port’s parts contiguous
Declaration/order as authored in the binding request
Any order (service must not depend on part order)
open_points.default_guess: Port-name Unicode order, with `many` file elements in list order inside that port.

open_points.subject: A15 rule 1 record write order for simultaneous non-executable mapped elements
open_points.text: "Records of nodes that become non-executable together are written in `node_id` order."
open_points.question: If multiple elements of the same mapped node (same `node_id`, different `map_index`) become `upstream_failed`/`skipped_by_guard` together, what is the required write order among those element records?
options: Store whatever internal iteration order occurs
open_points.default_guess: `map_index` ascending, with no-`map_index` before indexed elements.

open_points.subject: A09 rule 1 credential-header collision check
open_points.text: "header names compare without regard to case ... an installation whose credential header has the name of a required header refuses to start."
open_points.question: Is the credential-vs-required-header name collision check also case-insensitive, or exact-case only?
open_points.default_guess: Case-insensitive collision check, matching the earlier header-name rule.
